question:
DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. During a recent outage, a network engineer discovered that host A started to experience intermittent connectivity, when Leaf102 was down. Drag and drop the code snippets from the bottom onto the boxes in the code to resolve the problem. Not all code snippets are used.
context:
Topology: POD1 (Leaf101, Leaf102) and POD2 (Leaf201, Leaf202) connect through Spine01/Spine02 to Host A and Host B.
LEAF-101# show vpc orphan-ports
Note:
-------::Going through port database. Please be patient.::-------
VLAN       Orphan Ports
-------    -------------------
500        Po2
501        Po2
502        Po2
503        Po2
imageNote: Diagram: Host B connects to Leaf201/Leaf202 (POD2), which connect via vPC peer link and cross-links to Spine01/Spine02; Spine01/Spine02 connect down to Leaf101/Leaf102 (POD1), which connect to Host A.
theory: In this vPC design, Host A's port channel shows up in show vpc orphan-ports, meaning it is attached to only one leaf instead of being dual-homed across both members of the vPC pair — exactly why the host loses connectivity whenever that single leaf is unavailable. Converting the interface into a genuine vPC member by adding the vpc keyword under the port channel, alongside spanning-tree port type edge trunk for a host-facing trunk port that shouldn't take on switch-to-switch loop-prevention roles, dual-homes Host A across both leaves so connectivity survives either one going down. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Orphan Ports and Dual-Homing Design)
